### Day 55: Mock 2 preparation (Phase 3, week 8)

**What we learn today:** no new topic list and no new chunks. The pre-mock warm-up (3.3): five random prompts, each from a different engine (seen practice), first two sentences only; then the 10 core reactions and the 12 core reason pairs from the English cue. Then one short task of each type.

**Why it matters for the exam:** Mock 2 tomorrow is a full set. When the templates are warm, the first sentence of every task comes without thinking, and a fixed first sentence is the plan's first rescue rule against freezing (2.8).

**How we learn it (60 min):**
- 0–8 Review: cards from Days 25, 41, 48, 52 and 54.
- 8–16 Five random prompts, each from a different engine: read the card, say the first two sentences, next card.
- 16–22 The 10 core reactions and the 12 core reason pairs from the English cue, fast.
- 22–36 One task of each speaking type, timed and recorded. Tick the points only; no redo.
- 36–50 One formal writing task (14 min).
- 50–58 Notice routine, 8 minutes.
- 58–60 Check with the helper: tomorrow's prompts are ready, with a timer, a recorder and a quiet room for about 2.5 hours.

**Speaking output:**
- Berätta, 1 min prep + 1.5 min: *Berätta om en plats som du tycker om.* (Tell about a place you like.)
- Call, 6 turns × 20 s (the helper improvises, or you write 6 questions first): *Ring simhallen och fråga om simkurser för barn.* (Call the swimming hall and ask about swimming courses for children.)
- Voicemail, 20 s: *Du kan inte komma på fotbollsträningen i kväll. Lämna ett meddelande till tränaren.* (You can't come to football practice tonight. Leave the coach a message.)
- Three reactions, 20 s prep + 25 s each: *Din vän har fått tvillingar.* (Your friend has had twins.) / *Din kollegas plånbok är borta.* (Your colleague's wallet is missing.) / *En granne tackar dig för att du hjälpte honom.* (A neighbour thanks you for helping him.)
- Opinion, 1 min prep + 1.5 min: *Påstående: Det är bättre att ha många korta semestrar än en lång.* (Many short holidays are better than one long one.)

**Writing output:** *Du glömde en blå väska i omklädningsrummet på simhallen i går. Skriv till simhallen. Beskriv väskan, fråga om de har hittat den och ge dina kontaktuppgifter.* (You left a blue bag in the changing room at the swimming hall yesterday. Describe it, ask if they found it, give your contact details. T12, formal.) Required points (6): formal opening; what, when and where; a description (2 details); the question; contact details; formal closing.

**Done when (Green / Amber / Red):** Green = each of the five prompts gets two fitting first sentences, and all 5 speaking tasks and the formal task give all their points, on your own. Targets (not gates): about 8 minutes for the five prompts; the 10 core reactions and the 12 core reason pairs from the English cue (a miss is a card to review, not a fail); every task in time. No new cards except error cards.

**Typical errors to watch:**
- Learning new material the day before a mock. Today is recall only.
- A voicemail over 20 s. About 30 words is this plan's guide for 20 seconds (Day 84).
- Answering thanks with another *Tack!* → *Ingen orsak!* (reaction 18)

markdown:
### Day 56: Mock 2, a full mock day (Phase 3, week 8)

**What we learn today:** nothing new: this is the full four-weekly mock (section 6.2), with no new cards except the mock's error cards. Mock 2 is a progress check, so printed prompts may be used (plan 6.2): the blocks below are seen practice, and the helper changes their details. Fresh prompts from the teacher are better if they exist.

**Why it matters for the exam:** It runs the speaking and writing formats back to back under time, which builds stamina for a test day of about 5 hours including breaks [Official]. Mock 2 is a progress check and gates nothing: the Phase 3 exit test (Days 62–63) gates the phase, and only Mock 3 and later mocks count towards booking (6.4).

**How we learn it (2 to 2.5 hours; split into two sittings if needed, speaking first):**
- 0–5 Set up: timer, recorder, prompts face down. Paper only for the preparation minutes.
- 5–35 Speaking set S1–S6, back to back, recorded.
- 35–40 Break.
- 40–100 Writing set: W1 15 min, W2 25 min, W3 20 min [Plan's own]. Typed, no spelling help, no dictionary.
- 100–105 Break.
- 105–125 Listening and reading: 2 unseen easy-news clips (3 facts and every number for each) and 2 unseen notices (5 questions each: what, when, where, for whom, cost or condition), scored against the text.
- 125–145 Count (6.3). The teacher rates every task first; then you count points per task, time, word counts, engine errors and the listening and reading percentage. Where the counts differ, the teacher's count stands. Make the mock's error cards and send the teacher pack.

**Speaking output (seen practice):**
- S1, Berätta, 1 min prep + 1.5 min: *Berätta om en vanlig dag i ditt liv.* (Tell about an ordinary day in your life.)
- S2, buyer call, 6 turns × 20 s. Section 6.2 alternates the roles and Mock 3 is a seller call, so Mock 2 is a buyer call. Card: *Du har sett en annons om en begagnad mikrovågsugn. Ring säljaren. Fråga om ålder, skick och pris, försök få ett lägre pris och bestäm när du kan hämta den.* (Call about a used microwave: age, condition, price; try to get it cheaper; agree when to collect it.) The other voice: 1 *Hej, det är Leena.* 2 *Ja, den finns kvar.* 3 *Den är fyra år gammal och fungerar bra.* 4 *Jag vill ha 40 euro.* 5 *Hmm, jag kan ta 35 euro, men inte mindre.* 6 *Okej. När vill du hämta den?*
- S3, complaint call, 6 turns × 20 s. Card: *Du har beställt en ny säng från en möbelaffär. Den skulle komma i går, men ingen kom. Ring affären.* (You ordered a new bed. It should have come yesterday, but nobody came. Call the shop.) The other voice: 1 *Möbelaffären, hej.* 2 *Vad gäller det?* 3 *Har du ordernumret?* 4 *Jag ser att leveransen är flyttad till nästa vecka.* 5 *Tyvärr kan vi inte komma tidigare.* 6 *Jag ska se vad jag kan göra. Vi ringer dig i eftermiddag.*
- S4, voicemail, 20 s: *Du har bokat ett bord på en restaurang i kväll, men du kan inte komma. Lämna ett meddelande till restaurangen.* (You booked a table for tonight but can't come.)
- S5, three reactions, 20 s prep + 25 s each: *Din granne berättar att hon har fått ett barn.* (Your neighbour has had a baby.) / *Din vän har förlorat jobbet.* (Your friend has lost their job.) / *En kollega tackar dig för att du hjälpte henne med en presentation.* (A colleague thanks you for helping with a presentation.)
- S6, opinion, 1 min prep + 1.5 min: *Påstående: Barn borde inte ha läxor. Håller du med? Motivera din åsikt.* (Children should not have homework. Do you agree?)

**Writing output (seen practice):**
- W1, informal, 15 min, about 50–80 words [Teacher, unofficial]: *Du har flyttat till en ny lägenhet. Skriv till din vän Sara och bjud henne på middag. Berätta lite om lägenheten, föreslå en dag och en tid, och skriv hur hon hittar dit.* (You have moved. Invite Sara to dinner: a little about the flat, a day and time, how to get there.) Points (6): opening; the flat (1–2 details); the invitation with day and time; how to get there; a reply-by question; closing.
- W2, letter to the editor, 25 min, about 100–150 words: *Skriv en insändare: Alla borde jobba bara fyra dagar i veckan. Skriv din åsikt och ge minst tre skäl.* (Everyone should work only four days a week.) Points (8): topic line; opinion; reason 1; reason 2; reason 3; an example; the other view; a matching conclusion.
- W3, formal complaint, 20 min, about 50–80 words: *Du har fått en faktura från en trädgårdsfirma. Du tycker att den är för hög. Skriv till firman. Skriv vilken faktura det gäller, ge minst två skäl, föreslå ett rimligt belopp och ge dina kontaktuppgifter.* (A garden firm's bill is too high.) Points (7): which bill (number, date, amount); reason 1; reason 2; a suitable amount; what you want; contact details; a formal opening and closing. The learner's amounts must add up, as in the Day 57 model.

**Done when:** every task is attempted (none left blank) and recorded in two places. Mock 2 is a progress check and gates nothing (6.4).
- **Green / Amber / Red per subtest** (the rule above Day 15, applied to each subtest's tasks together), in the table you started on Day 28. It is an early skill signal, not a decision: the strongest pair may start to show, but the pair, the date and the sitting are still chosen only at booking time (4.7).

| Subtest | Tasks | Mock 1 (Day 28) | Mock 2: G / A / R | Top 1–2 mistakes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Speaking | S1–S6 | | | |
| Writing | W1–W3 | | | |
| Listening | 2 clips | | | |
| Reading | 2 notices | | | |

- **Booking-gate checks** [Plan's own, 6.4], recorded for practice only: every required point covered in every task; every task finished in time; a teacher rating of A or B ("understandable with some errors" or better) on every task. Engine errors per text are counted and tracked on the error list, not gated. Listening and reading about 70% or more, counted only on teacher- or helper-written questions in the three formats (multiple choice, true/false, short open answers) and only relevant for a pair with listening or reading. Write the numbers in your progress record next to Mock 1. Day 57, the error clinic, starts from this mock's errors.

**Typical errors to watch:**
- In S2, no offer or no pick-up time. The card asks for both.
- In S3, missing *flyttad* (moved) in the voice's line. It changes what you must protest about.
- W2 with only two reasons, or W3 with no amount or no contact details. These are required points in the official samples [Official sample].

It turns Mock 2's errors into work: the 12-sentence engine drill (wrong, then right) plus 2 new correct sentences for each of your own top 3 error types, then a repair-call redo (*Ditt kylskåp är fortfarande trasigt …*, T4, 7 points) and a 15-minute bill complaint to a painting firm (7 points, amounts that add up).
Any error type seen 3 or more times this week is marked red (3.6). This is the format every later fix day copies.
**Done when (Green / Amber / Red):** Green = the call and the complaint each give all 7 points, with amounts that add up, on your own, and the drill sentences are written. The counts in 5.1 are targets, not gates.

[Unreviewed Swedish: have a teacher check it]

**Book practice (*Förbered dig för allmän språkexamen*, pointers only; descriptions are our own words):** 2 task(s) today. Each replaces one of today's own prompts, or the redo of one; if nothing fits, it waits for a 90-minute day (see the note at the top of this file).
- `p87-R4`: p. 87, Reagera 4 (phone), T4: Call payroll about a mistake in your pay
- `p96-D1`: p. 96-97, Dialog 1 (phone), T4: Call the library: overdue notice for a book you never borrowed; deny it.

---

**Full day plan (from the method, section 5.1)**

#### Day 57: error clinic after Mock 2

| Minutes | What you do |
|---|---|
| 0–10 | Review: your Mock 2 error cards. |
| 10–22 | **Engine drill.** Correct each of the 12 sentences below aloud. Then, for your own top 3 error types, write 2 new correct sentences each. |
| 22–37 | **Speaking: a repair call redo** with a new card (below). Use T4. Aim for all 7 points. |
| 37–52 | **Writing** (15 min, this plan's own limit): the bill complaint below, all four official-sample points. |
| 52–57 | Easy-news routine, shortened. |
| 57–60 | Error log. Mark any error type you saw about 3 or more times this week as **recurring** (3.6). Mark the day Green, Amber or Red (section 1). |

**The 12-sentence drill (wrong, then right):**

| # | Wrong | Right |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | *I morgon jag jobbar.* | *I morgon jobbar jag.* |
| 2 | *För det första det är billigt.* | *För det första är det billigt.* |
| 3 | *Jag inte kan komma.* | *Jag kan inte komma.* |
| 4 | *I dag kan inte jag komma.* (avoid: it stresses *jag*) | *I dag kan jag inte komma.* |
| 5 | *Jag vet att han kommer inte.* | *Jag vet att han inte kommer.* |
| 6 | *Problemet är att den fungerar inte.* | *Problemet är att den inte fungerar.* |
| 7 | *Jag undrar när börjar kursen.* | *Jag undrar när kursen börjar.* |
| 8 | *Jag vill att köpa en ny.* | *Jag vill köpa en ny.* |
| 9 | *Jag har köpte en telefon.* | *Jag har köpt en telefon.* |
| 10 | *Jag har köpt den i går.* | *Jag köpte den i går.* |
| 11 | *ett ny kylskåp / min problem* | *ett nytt kylskåp / mitt problem* |
| 12 | *Jag är jobbar här.* | *Jag jobbar här.* |

**Speaking card:** *Ditt kylskåp är fortfarande trasigt, fast det var på reparation förra veckan. Ring firman. Förklara problemet, protestera och säg vad du vill.*

**Writing prompt:** *Du har fått en faktura från en målerifirma. Du tycker att fakturan är för hög. Skriv till firman. Skriv vilken faktura det gäller, ge minst två skäl till att den är för hög, säg vilket belopp som är rimligt och ge dina kontaktuppgifter.*

**Required points (7):**
1. Which bill: number, date and amount.
2. Reason 1.
3. Reason 2.
4. A suitable amount.
5. What you want.
6. Contact details.
7. A formal opening and closing.

**Model:**
> *Hej! Jag skriver om faktura nummer 2087 från den 3 oktober på 1 200 euro. Fakturan är för hög av två skäl. För det första sa ni att arbetet skulle ta två dagar, men ni har tagit betalt för fyra dagar. För det andra har ni tagit betalt för färg som jag själv köpte. Jag tycker att 500 euro är rimligt. Kan ni skicka en ny faktura? Ni når mig på 040 123 4567. Med vänliga hälsningar, Alex Kumar*

**The arithmetic in the model:** 4 days at 250 euro, plus 200 euro of paint, makes 1 200 euro. The correct amount is 2 days at 250 euro, which is 500 euro. The model has about 77 words, inside the unofficial 50–80 target.

**Common errors (beyond the drill):**
- No amount, or no contact details. The official sample requires both.
- *för två veckor* when you mean "two weeks ago". The right form is *för två veckor sedan*.

**On a 90-minute day, also:** do the same complaint by phone, using the T4 and T5 lines.

markdown:
### Day 60: formal writing set (Phase 3, week 9)

**What we learn today:**
- Three formal templates at speed: T2 (*Jag skriver för att fråga om [___]. Jag undrar om [___]. Tack på förhand.*), T5 (*Jag skriver om faktura nummer [___] från den [datum]. Fakturan är för hög av två skäl.*) and T12 (*Jag vill anmäla att [___]. Det hände [___]. Kan ni [___]?*).
- The formal e-mail frame for all three (the opening and closing fit a formal e-mail, not a phone call): *Hej!* (or *Bästa mottagare,*) and a first line that says why you write, *Jag skriver angående [___].* (I am writing about …); T2 and T5 have their own first lines above. Close with *Ni når mig på [telefonnummer] eller [e-post].* *Med vänliga hälsningar, [för- och efternamn]*.
- One phone refusal (T8): *Tack, men jag behöver inget nytt abonnemang.* (Thanks, but I don't need a new subscription.)

**Why it matters for the exam:** One of the three writing sample tasks is formal: a complaint with which bill, at least two reasons, a suitable amount and contact details [Official sample]. Writing three formal texts in a row trains the points-first habit under time.

**How we learn it (60 min):**
- 0–6 Review: cards from Days 30, 46, 53, 57 and 59.
- 6–11 The call (seen practice), 4 turns × 20 s [Plan's practice limit], recorded.
- 11–47 Three formal texts, 12 minutes each [Plan's own: shorter than the 20-minute mock limit, to build speed]. Write each task's points as tick boxes first. Do the T5 bill complaint (D4) first.
- 47–55 Notice routine with an official letter, 8 minutes.
- 55–60 Error log.
- **Core and optional (third review):** a declared set day: three typed texts instead of one (an exception to load rule 5), still inside 60 minutes. Core = the call and the T5 bill complaint (D4), the official sample type. The T2 and T12 texts complete the set; if a text runs past 12 minutes, stop after two and do the third on the next 90-minute day or on Day 76. Green needs only the core tasks; rate the others too.
- **Load check:** 0 new patterns (the refusal line is Day 24's *…, men jag behöver …* with new words) · at most 3 new cards (error cards) · about 60 minutes (call 5, three texts 36, notice 8, review and log 11).

**Speaking output (seen practice):** G3: a salesperson phones and offers you a new mobile subscription; you don't want it. Points (4): acknowledge or thank; a clear no; a reason; a kind close.

**Writing output (seen practice):**

- T5, D4: a removal firm damaged your table and charged more hours than agreed. Points (7): which bill (number, date, amount); reason 1, the damage; reason 2, the hours; a suitable amount; what you want; contact details; formal opening and closing.

Model (J6): *Hej! Jag bor i lägenhet B 12 på Solvägen 5. Det har legat sopsäckar i trapphuset sedan i måndags. Det luktar illa, och barnen leker där. Kan ni ta bort soporna och prata med de boende? Ni når mig på 040 123 4567. Med vänliga hälsningar, Alex Kumar* (*en sopsäck* = a rubbish bag; *de boende* = the residents.)

2. G10 (work), 20 s prep + 25 s [Teacher, unofficial]: a colleague wants you to give a speech at the party; you don't want to. Points: thanks; a clear no; a reason; an alternative or a kind close.
3. I3 (health and wellbeing, T11), 30 s prep + 1 min [Plan's own]: a colleague sleeps badly; give advice. Points: at least 2 pieces of advice, each with a reason or example; a friendly close.

### Day 63: Phase 3 exit test, part 2 (Phase 3, week 9)

**What we learn today:** the other five exit prompts, then the count of all ten.

**Why it matters for the exam:** Phase 4 is timed full sets and mocks. Starting it with a function or topic that still fails only repeats that failure under time pressure.

**How we learn it (about 75 min):**
- 0–3 Set up as on Day 62.
- 3–15 Tasks 6–8, back to back, recorded.
- 15–40 Task 9, letter (25 min [Plan's own], about 100–150 words [Teacher, unofficial]).
- 40–60 Task 10, formal (20 min).
- 60–65 Rate all ten tasks Green, Amber or Red, and note points per task, time and engine errors per text for the record (6.3). Put all ten in the teacher pack.
- 65–75 All overdue cards.

**Speaking output (seen practice):**
6. L5 (me and my background), 1 min prep + 1.5 min: a holiday or festival (*en högtid*) in your home country.
7. J5 (society, T12), call, 6 turns × 20 s: the street lamp outside your house does not work; call the municipality. Points: who; what; where (address); since when; why it is a problem; what you want; contact details.
8. K5 (travel), 1 min prep + 1.5 min: *Det är bättre att resa med tåg än med flyg.* Points: opinion; 2 reasons; an example; the other view; a matching conclusion.

**Writing output (seen practice):**
9. K6 (society), letter: all adults should learn a new language. Points (8): topic line; opinion; 3 reasons; an example; the other view; a matching conclusion.
10. A10 (shops and services): write to a restaurant; book a table for eight on Saturday and ask about vegetarian food. Points: day; time; number of people; the vegetarian question; contact details; formal opening and closing.

**Listening and reading:** one clip after the count, if time allows.

**Done when:** all ten tasks are rated Green, Amber or Red (rule above Day 15).

**Phase-exit rule** (Days 62 and 63 together, 10 tasks; section 4.4 as revised on 16 November 2026): the phase is passed when **at most 1 task is Red and no Red is a misunderstood question on a required point**. Targets (not gates): every required point covered; every task finished in time; engine errors per written text counted and kept on the error list; a teacher rating of A or B ("understandable with some errors" or better). The teacher's rating can change a mark. With no outside rater the result is provisional (3.5).
- **After a pass:** a Red task (at most one) is repeated with new details in the next day or two, using the matching day of Days 43–61; then Phase 4 starts with Day 64. Amber tasks put their top 1–2 mistakes on the error list.
- **If it is not passed** (2 or more Reds, or a Red that misunderstood a question on a required point): add at most one extra week of topic days for the Red topics or functions (repeat the matching Days 43–61 with new prompts), then retest those tasks before Day 64.

**Typical errors to watch:**
- *På Diwali vi tänder ljus.* → *På Diwali tänder vi ljus.* (G1)
- *Jag undrar om har ni vegetarisk mat.* → *Jag undrar om ni har vegetarisk mat.* (G3)
- In J5, no address. The card's "where" is a required point.

- S2, seller, 6 turns × 20 s: B6, you sell a winter jacket. The voice: 1 *Hej, jag ringer om vinterjackan i annonsen. Finns den kvar?* 2 *Vilken storlek och färg är den?* 3 *Är den varm?* 4 *Vad kostar den?* 5 *Kan du ta 30 euro?* 6 *Var kan vi träffas?* Points (6): still available; size and colour; condition; price; an answer to the offer; a meeting place and time.

Förklara problemet, protestera och säg vad du vill.* (Your vacuum cleaner was repaired but still stops after five minutes.) The voice: 1 *Kundtjänst, hej.* 2 *Vad gäller det?* 3 *När var den på reparation?* 4 *Du kan lämna in den igen nästa vecka.* 5 *Tyvärr kan vi inte ge dig en ny.* 6 *Jag ska fråga min chef. Vi ringer dig på fredag.* Points (6): who; what it concerns; the fault; that it was already repaired, and when; a protest with a reason; what you want, with a time limit.

Fråga när kursen börjar, vad den kostar och hur man anmäler sig.* The voice: 1 *Medborgarinstitutet, god morgon.* 2 *Ja, vi har en kurs för nybörjare. markdown:
### Day 67: teacher feedback day (Phase 4, week 10)

**What we learn today:** the fix routine (3.6) applied to set A. Turn the teacher's sheets and your error log into 3 targeted drills, then redo the weakest speaking task and the weakest writing task of set A with one detail changed. With no feedback back yet, use your own count and mark today's result provisional.

**How to build the 3 drills:**
1. List every error from set A in the log by type (G1–G10, word choice, missing point, over time), adding the teacher's top 3 per task.
2. Take the 3 types with the highest "times seen". A type seen 3 or more times this week is red.
3. Make one 4-minute drill per type: a word-order type → 10 new sentences of that pattern on this week's topics; a missing point → 5 old cards, points as tick boxes, then one sentence per point only; over time → cut each answer to the 30-word voicemail guide or 2 sentences per call turn, then re-time it.

**Worked example (G2, *inte* in a subordinate clause).** Log lines: Day 64 S1 *eftersom den är inte dyr*; Day 65 W3 *att vi har inte köpt nya maskiner*; Day 66 call *om jag kan inte komma*. Seen 3 times: red. Drill, 10 sentences, *inte* before the verb after *eftersom, att, om, som*:
1. *Jag ringer eftersom dammsugaren inte fungerar.*
2. *Jag skriver eftersom jag inte har fått pengarna tillbaka.*
3. *Problemet är att fakturan inte stämmer.* (*stämma* = be correct)
4. *Jag hoppas att det inte tar lång tid.*
5. *Jag vet att ni inte har tid i dag.*
Then 5 more of your own; the teacher checks them in the next pack.

**Why it matters for the exam:** "Basic structures often wrong" is a level-2 sign [Official]. Fixing the three most frequent errors removes more mistakes than any new content.

**How we learn it (60 min):**
- 0–6 Review: cards from Days 37, 53, 60, 64 and 66.
- 6–10 Read the sheets; count; pick the top 3.
- 10–22 The 3 drills, 4 minutes each.
- 22–34 Redo the weakest speaking task of set A with one new detail. Record; compare with Day 64.
- 34–49 Redo the weakest writing task with one new detail (15 min).
- 49–57 Easy-news routine, 8 minutes.
- 57–60 Error log; error cards for at most 3 of the drilled sentences (3.3).

**Speaking output:** the weakest set A task again, for example S3 with a coffee machine instead of a vacuum cleaner.

**Writing output:** the weakest set A text again, for example W3 with a water bill instead of electricity.

**Listening and reading:** easy-news routine.

**Done when (Green / Amber / Red):** Green = both redos give every point, on your own, and the 3 drills are done. Targets (not gates): every drill sentence correct; the drilled error types gone from the redos (if one is still there, that redo is Amber: keep the type on the error list).

**Typical errors to watch:**
- Redoing the best task instead of the weakest. The rating sheet decides.
- Drilling 10 sentences that copy one model. Change the subject and the verb each time.
- *Jag hoppas att det blir inte dyrt.* → *Jag hoppas att det inte blir dyrt.* (G2)

### Day 68: mixed prompts 2 (Phase 4, week 10)

**What we learn today:** no new chunks. Card words for today's prompts: *en påminnelse* (a reminder letter), *en avgift* (a fee), *smutsig* (dirty), *en dusch* (a shower), *pengar tillbaka* (money back), *delvis* (partly). And the adapt rule from Day 48: underline the points, choose the main engine and borrow moves from others where the card needs them, fill every slot, delete what is not asked.

**Why it matters for the exam:** A reaction, a phone complaint and a formal message are all sample or practice formats [Official sample; Teacher, unofficial]. Mixing them on cards you have not practised is closer to a test than any drilled day.

**How we learn it (60 min):**
- 0–6 Review: cards from Days 38, 54, 61, 65 and 67.
- 6–10 The 10 core reactions from the English cue (the other 20 are recognise only).
- 10–22 Three reactions and the call (seen practice), back to back, recorded.
- 22–28 Listen once for points.
- 28–48 The formal task (20 min, the mock limit).
- 48–56 Notice routine, 8 minutes.
- 56–60 Error log.
- **Core and optional (third review):** core = the C10 hotel call and the formal task; the three reactions are extra volume in the same 12 minutes.

**Speaking output (seen practice):**
- Reactions, 20 s prep + 25 s each [Plan's own]: a) *Din kollega har sprungit ett maraton.* (Your colleague ran a marathon.) b) *Din granne har tappat sina nycklar och kan inte komma in i lägenheten.* (Your neighbour lost her keys and can't get in.) c) *En vän frågar om du vill följa med och simma i morgon bitti, men du jobbar.* (Refuse.) Points per reaction (3).
- C10, call, 6 turns × 20 s: you stayed at a hotel; the room was dirty and the shower did not work. Points: who; your dates; problem 1; problem 2; a protest; ask for part of the money back; a close.

**Writing output (seen practice):** D5: you paid a bill but got a reminder with a 10-euro fee. Points (7): which bill; when you paid; the reminder and the fee; ask them to remove the fee; what else you want (for example a new bill without the fee); contact details; formal opening and closing.

**Listening and reading:** notice routine.

**Done when (Green / Amber / Red):** Green = each reaction fits the news with its 3 points, the call gives all its points and the formal text all 7, on your own. Targets (not gates): no turn over 20 s; engine errors go on the error list (aim: 2 or fewer).

**Typical errors to watch:**
- *Jag vill inte att betala avgiften.* → *Jag vill inte betala avgiften.* (G4)
- In c), a refusal with no reason or other time. Use core reaction 28 with a reason and T8's other time: *Tyvärr kan jag inte, eftersom jag jobbar. Kanske en annan gång?*
- In C10, only one problem. The card has two.

### Day 69: opinion and person (Phase 4, week 10)

**What we learn today:** the two long talks and the letter, at full length. T13 (the five steps in 2.2) and T14 with the six-point talk plan. Reasons that fit today's letter: 5 *Det är bra för miljön.* 31 *Det blir mycket skräp.* against: 6 *Det är praktiskt.* (said as the other view) and 36 *Det passar inte alla.*

**Why it matters for the exam:** The letter to the editor needs at least three reasons [Official sample]; the person talk is 1 min prep + 1.5 min [Official sample]; the opinion talk is a practice format of the same length [Teacher, unofficial].

**How we learn it (60 min; trimmed from about 65 by the third review):**
- 0–6 Review: cards from Days 39, 55, 62, 66 and 68.
- 6–10 The T13 and T14 skeletons aloud; one *Till exempel* sentence for each reason above.
- 10–28 Two talks, recorded; listen twice; redo the weaker once.
- 28–48 The letter (20 minutes, a little under the 25-minute mock limit, as 3.1 asks of daily writing), points first.
- 48–56 Easy-news routine, 8 minutes.
- 56–60 Error log.
- **Core and optional:** core = the opinion talk and the letter. The person talk is the second task; if the talks run over, keep it for Day 70's re-recording.

**Speaking output (seen practice), both 1 min prep + 1.5 min [Plan's own prompts]:**
- *Berätta om en granne eller en kollega som du tycker om.* (Tell about a neighbour or colleague you like.) The six-point plan.
- *Påstående: Alla borde ha en dag i veckan utan mobiltelefon. Håller du med? Motivera din åsikt.* (Everyone should have one day a week without a mobile phone.) Points (6): opinion; 2 reasons; an example; the other view; a matching conclusion.

**Writing output (seen practice):** [Plan's own] *Skriv en insändare: Affärerna borde sluta sälja plastpåsar. Skriv din åsikt och ge minst tre skäl.* (Shops should stop selling plastic bags.) Points (8): topic line; opinion; 3 reasons; an example; the other view; a matching conclusion; about 100–150 words. (*en plastpåse*; in Finland *en plastkasse* may be more common: ask the teacher.)

**Listening and reading:** easy-news routine.

**Done when (Green / Amber / Red):** Green = the opinion talk and the letter give all their points, on your own, and the person talk too if you did it. Targets (not gates): each talk at least 1 minute 15 seconds (aim 1.5, about 120 words at the practice pace); the letter about 100–150 words; engine errors go on the error list (aim: 2 or fewer).

**Typical errors to watch:**
- *För det tredje det blir mindre skräp.* → *För det tredje blir det mindre skräp.* (G1)
- *Jag har känt henne sedan fem år.* → *Jag har känt henne i fem år.* (G9)
- Using reason 18 *Man behöver ingen bil* in a talk about phones. Use only reasons the topic supports.

### Day 70: light day (Phase 4, week 10)

**What we learn today:** nothing new. All overdue cards, then your weakest task re-recorded from memory with one new detail. The teacher's sheets from Day 67, or your own count, decide which task is weakest. Six days earlier was Day 64, so a set A task fits the light-day rule (3.1).

**Why it matters for the exam:** Re-doing an old task with a change keeps a format ready without memorising one fixed answer (3.4).

**How we learn it (about 35 min):**
- 0–15 All overdue cards.
- 15–25 The weakest task, from memory, one detail changed (a new item, day or reason). Record it; listen once for points.
- 25–35 Easy-news routine with one new clip.

**Speaking output:** the task above, inside its original time limit.

**Writing output:** none (light day).

**Listening and reading:** one new clip: 3 facts and every number.

**Done when (Green / Amber / Red):** Green = the re-recorded task, with one detail changed, gives all its points, on your own. Targets (not gates): no turn over its limit; the overdue cards cleared.

**Typical errors to watch:**
- Re-recording the same words as Day 64. Change at least one detail.
- *I går jag glömde …* → *I går glömde jag …* (G1)

markdown:
### Day 71: full speaking set B and an event message (Phase 4, week 11)

Day 71: see section 5.1 of the plan.
It runs speaking set B timed with no pauses: a) *Berätta om en vän som du har känt länge.* (six-point plan), b) a seller call about a bike, c) a repair call about a computer (T4, 6 points), d) a 20-second late voicemail to Sara. Then a 15-minute event message (what, when, where, two details, an invitation question, opening and closing: 8 points).
The whole set goes in the teacher pack. Week 11's top-3 error drill (6.1) is folded into Day 72, the fix day.
**Done when (Green / Amber / Red):** Green = every speaking task and the event message give all their points, on your own. The times and counts in 5.1 are targets, not gates.

[Unreviewed Swedish: have a teacher check it]

**Book practice (*Förbered dig för allmän språkexamen*, pointers only; descriptions are our own words):** 1 task(s) today. Each replaces one of today's own prompts, or the redo of one; if nothing fits, it waits for a 90-minute day (see the note at the top of this file).
- `p85-D4`: p. 85-86, Dialog 4, T15: Coffee-room chat after a business trip: where, what you did, hotel, how you feel

---

**Full day plan (from the method, section 5.1)**

#### Day 71: full speaking set B and an event message

| Minutes | What you do |
|---|---|
| 0–5 | Say the first line of T1, T3, T4, T9 and T14 aloud. |
| 5–28 | **Full speaking set B, timed, with no pauses between tasks:** a) person, b) seller call, c) repair call, d) voicemail. Record all of it. |
| 28–36 | Listen to each task twice and tick its checklist. |
| 36–51 | **Writing** (15 min): the event message below. |
| 51–57 | Easy-news routine, shortened. |
| 57–60 | Error log. Put the set in the teacher pack. |

**a) Person** (1 min prep + 1.5 min [Official sample timing])

**Prompt:** *Berätta om en vän som du har känt länge.*

**Six-point talk plan** [Plan's own coaching]:
1. Who the person is.
2. How long you have known them.
3. What they look like and what they are like.
4. What you do together.
5. Why they are important.
6. A memory or a wish.

**Model:**
> *Jag vill berätta om min vän Ravi. Vi har känt varandra i femton år. Vi gick i samma skola i Pune. Ravi är lång och har kort svart hår. Han är rolig och mycket hjälpsam. Nu bor han i Bangalore och jobbar som läkare. Vi brukar prata i telefon en gång i veckan. När jag flyttade till Finland hjälpte han mig mycket. Han gav mig många bra råd och ringde mig varje dag den första månaden. Han är viktig för mig eftersom han alltid finns där när jag behöver honom. Nästa sommar vill jag resa till Indien och träffa honom.*

**b) Seller call** (6 turns; an official sample task type, where you are the seller)

**Situation card:** *Du säljer din cykel. En köpare ringer. Svara på frågorna. Föreslå en tid och säg var du bor.*

| Turn | Other voice | Model answer |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | *Hej, jag ringer om cykeln i annonsen. Finns den kvar?* | *Hej! Ja, den finns kvar. Det här är Alex.* |
| 2 | *Hur gammal är den?* | *Den är tre år gammal, men jag har inte använt den så mycket.* |
| 3 | *Är den i bra skick?* | *Ja, den är i mycket bra skick. Jag bytte däcken i våras.* |
| 4 | *Vad kostar den?* | *Den kostar 150 euro. En lampa och ett lås ingår i priset.* |
| 5 | *Kan du sälja den för 100 euro?* | *Nej, tyvärr. Men du kan få den för 130 euro.* |
| 6 | *Okej. När kan jag komma och titta på den?* | *Du kan komma i morgon efter klockan sex. Jag bor på Solvägen 5 i Esbo. Ring när du är här!* |

**c) Repair call** (6 turns; use T4; no model given)

**Situation card:** *Din dator är fortfarande trasig, fast den har varit på reparation. Ring datorbutiken. Förklara problemet, protestera och säg vad du vill att butiken gör.*

The other voice says, one line per turn:
1. *Datorbutiken, hej.*
2. *Vad gäller det?*
3. *Vad är felet?*
4. *Vi kan skicka den på reparation igen. Det tar tre veckor.*
5. *Det kan vi tyvärr inte lova.*
6. *Okej, jag ska prata med min chef. Vi ringer dig.*

**Required points (6):**
1. Who you are.
2. What it concerns.
3. The fault.
4. That it was already repaired.
5. A protest with a reason.
6. What you want: a new computer or your money back, with a time limit.

**d) Voicemail** (20 s [Official sample timing])

**Situation card:** *Du ska träffa din vän Sara klockan sex, men du blir sen. Lämna ett meddelande.*

**Model:**
> *Hej Sara, det är Alex. Förlåt, jag blir ungefär en kvart försenad, eftersom bussen inte har kommit. Jag är där kvart över sex. Kan du vänta på mig vid ingången? Vi ses!*

**Writing prompt** [Official sample task type]: *Skriv ett meddelande till din vän. Berätta om ett evenemang som du vill gå på. Skriv vad det är, när och var det är, och ge två andra detaljer. Fråga om din vän vill följa med.*

**Required points (8):**
1. Opening.
2. What.
3. When.
4. Where.
5. Detail 1.
6. Detail 2.
7. Invitation question.
8. Closing.

**Model:**
> *Hej Sara! Har du hört om matfestivalen i parken vid järnvägsstationen? Den är på lördag, från klockan tolv till sex. Det finns mat från många länder, till exempel Indien, Thailand och Mexiko. Inträdet är gratis, men maten kostar några euro. Jag tänkte gå dit vid två. Vill du följa med? Skriv till mig före fredag! Kram, Alex*

**Common errors:**

| Wrong | Right | Why |
|---|---|---|
| *Förlåt, jag blir sen eftersom bussen kommer inte.* | *… eftersom bussen inte kommer.* | G2 |
| *Jag bytte däcken för två månader.* | *Jag bytte däcken för två månader sedan.* | G9 |
| An event message with no "where" | Add the place | A missing point |
| In the seller call, not saying where you live | Say it | A missing point; the card asks for it |

**On a 90-minute day, also:** do three reactions and one buyer call (appendix B).

markdown:
### Day 72: fix day (Phase 4, week 11)

**What we learn today:** the fix routine (Day 67) on set B and this week's log: count the error types, take the top 3, make 3 four-minute drills, then redo 2 speaking tasks and 1 writing task with new details.

**Worked example (missing point).** Log lines: Day 71 b) seller call, no address (the card says *säg var du bor*); Day 71 event message, no "where"; Day 68 C10, only one of the two problems. Type "missing point", seen 3 times: red. Drill (4 minutes):
1. Take 5 old cards (Days 54 a, 61 b, 64 S2, 50 writing, 65 W1).
2. For each, write the points as tick boxes in 30 seconds.
3. Say or type **one sentence per point** and nothing else, about 1 minute per card.
4. Add a capital-letter line to the top of the template card (3.6, rule 4). T3: SÄG VAR DU BOR: *Jag bor på [Solvägen 5] i [Esbo].* T6: SKRIV VAR: *Det är [i parken vid stationen].*

The other two drills follow the Day 67 recipe for their type.

**Why it matters for the exam:** The sample tasks list their required points [Official sample], and a missing point is the one error no grammar can repair. Point-checking is a habit, so it is drilled like grammar.

**How we learn it (60 min):**
- 0–6 Review: cards from Days 42, 58, 65, 69 and 71.
- 6–10 Read the teacher's set B sheets (or count yourself: provisional); pick the top 3.
- 10–22 The 3 drills, 4 minutes each.
- 22–36 Redo the 2 weakest set B speaking tasks with new details. Record; tick the points.
- 36–49 Redo 1 writing task: the Day 71 event message or the Day 69 letter, whichever scored lower (13 min [Plan's own]).
- 49–57 Notice routine, 8 minutes.
- 57–60 Error log.

**Speaking output:** for example set B c) with a broken phone instead of a computer, and d) with a new reason and time.

**Writing output:** the lower-scoring text, with a new event or a new statement.

**Listening and reading:** notice routine.

**Done when (Green / Amber / Red):** Green = both speaking redos and the writing redo give every point, on your own, and the 3 drills are done. Targets (not gates): every drill sentence correct; no drilled error type in the redos (if one is still there, that redo is Amber: keep the type on the error list).

**Typical errors to watch:**
- *Jag bor i Solvägen 5.* → *Jag bor på Solvägen 5.* (a street address takes *på*, as in T3)
- *Du kan komma i morgon efter sex klockan.* → *… efter klockan sex.*
- Redoing a task with the same details as before. Change at least one; otherwise you are memorising one answer (3.4).

### Day 73: full writing set B (Phase 4, week 11)

**What we learn today:** no new content. Three reactions (today's one speaking task, 4 minutes), then one writing set, set B, at the mock limits: W1 15 min, W2 25 min, W3 20 min [Plan's own limits]. The two book tasks replace one reaction and W2's statement, so they add no time. The day runs about 80 minutes, a declared set-day exception to load rule 6 (see the Part 3 note); do not split the set across two days.

**Why it matters for the exam:** All three writing sample types in one sitting [Official sample]; this second full set shows whether set A's errors have gone.

**Speaking output (seen practice):** reactions, 20 s prep + 25 s each [Plan's own]: a) today, the book task p87-R11 (a colleague leaves on maternity leave; Book practice below). The printed a), *Din chef säger att du har gjort ett mycket bra jobb i år.* (Your manager praises your work.), stays a spare. b) *Din kollega berättar att hon inte fick lägenheten som hon ville ha.* (Your colleague didn't get the flat she wanted.) c) *En granne ber om ursäkt för att hans hund skällde hela natten.* (A neighbour apologises because his dog barked all night.) Points per reaction (3).

**Writing output (seen practice):**
- W1 [Plan's own]: *Din vän vill träffas i helgen. Skriv och föreslå en utflykt till en nationalpark. Skriv när och var ni träffas, hur ni åker dit och vad ni ska ta med.* Points (7): opening; the trip; when; where you meet; how you travel; what to bring; closing with a question.
- W2, letter: the topic is the book task p37-OI (Book practice below: how well Finns dress, compared with other countries). It replaces the printed statement [Plan's own] *Skriv en insändare: Det är bättre att resa i sitt eget land än utomlands. Skriv din åsikt och ge minst tre skäl.*, which stays a spare for the cycle after Day 84. Points (8), as on Day 65.

Model (W1): *Hej Sara! Vill du följa med på en utflykt till en nationalpark på lördag? Vi kan träffas vid järnvägsstationen klockan nio. Vi åker buss dit, och resan tar ungefär en timme. Där kan vi gå fem kilometer och grilla korv. Ta med varma kläder, bra skor och något att dricka. Vad säger du? Skriv till mig före torsdag! Kram, Alex* (about 65 words)

**Listening and reading:** easy-news routine.

markdown:
### Day 74: outside functions (Phase 4, week 11)

**What we learn today:**
- T16 directions, as a chain: *Gå ut från huset och ta till vänster.* (Go out of the building and turn left.) *Gå rakt fram i ungefär hundra meter.* (Go straight on for about 100 metres.) *Ta sedan till höger vid busshållplatsen.* (Then turn right at the bus stop.) *Affären ligger mittemot skolan.* (The shop is opposite the school.) *Det tar fem minuter att gå.* (It takes five minutes to walk.)
- T11 advice: *Jag tycker att du ska [___]. Om jag var du skulle jag [___]. Det är en bra idé att [___].*
- T12 report: *Jag vill anmäla att [en bil har stått framför porten i tre dagar].* (*en port* = the front door of a building.)

**Why it matters for the exam:** In one practice book, 8 of 21 writing tasks fall outside the top five functions [Book count]. These moves stop an unusual card from becoming a blank answer.

**How we learn it (60 min):**
- 0–6 Review: cards from Days 44, 60, 67, 71 and 73.
- 6–15 The three line sets aloud; a ladder (3.2) on the directions chain with your own street.
- 15–30 Two speaking prompts (seen practice), recorded; listen once; redo the weaker.
- 30–45 The writing prompt (15 min).
- 45–53 Notice routine, 8 minutes.
- 53–60 Error log; error cards only (at most 3): every line today is a Day 36, 37 or 38a pattern with new words.
- **Core and optional (third review):** core = L8, the directions (the least practised function: only Day 38a so far), and the I8 advice e-mail. J9, the report call, is the second speaking task: do it if the block has time (it usually does), otherwise keep it for Day 76.
- **Load check:** 0 new patterns · at most 3 new cards (error cards) · about 50 minutes (line sets 5, two prompts with listen and redo 10.5, e-mail 15, notice 8, review and log 11); the spare minutes go to the J9 redo.

**Speaking output (seen practice):**
- L8 (T16), 30 s prep + 1 min [Plan's own]: describe the way from your home to the nearest shop. Points (5): the start; at least 3 direction steps; a landmark; how long it takes; a close.
- J9 (T12), call, 6 turns × 20 s: a car has been parked in front of your building's door for three days; call the landlord. Points: who and where you live; what; since when; why it is a problem; what you want; contact details.

**Writing output (seen practice):** I8 (T11): a friend wants to save money; write three suggestions. Points (5): opening; 3 suggestions, each with a reason or an example; closing.

**Listening and reading:** notice routine.

**Done when (Green / Amber / Red):** Green = the directions give all 5 points and the advice e-mail all 5, on your own; the call, if you did it, is rated the same way. Targets (not gates): 1 minute for the directions; engine errors go on the error list (aim: 2 or fewer).

**Typical errors to watch:**
- *Om jag var du jag skulle laga mat hemma.* → *Om jag var du skulle jag laga mat hemma.* (G1)
- *Bilen står där sedan tre dagar.* → *Bilen har stått där i tre dagar.* (G6, G9)
- Directions with no landmark. One fixed point (*banken, skolan, busshållplatsen*) makes them usable.

Targets, not pass marks: every instruction word, and about 18 of the 20 others (the E1 figures); a missed word becomes a card.

**Why it matters for the exam:** Every instruction is in Swedish [Official]; a misread instruction costs points before your Swedish is tested (2.6). This is the second timed listening and reading set, so its score can be compared with Day 66.

**How we learn it (60 min):**

### Day 81: fix day (Phase 4, week 12)

**What we learn today:** the fix routine (Day 67) on set C and Day 80, then redo 2 speaking tasks and 1 writing task from set C with new details. These are the last errors to remove before Mock 3.

**Worked example (G6, past or perfect).** Log lines: Day 78 S3 *Jag har beställt den i måndags*; Day 79 W3 *Jag har hyrt bilen den 10 mars*; Day 80 call *Jag har varit där förra veckan*. Seen 3 times: red. The rule: a finished time (*i måndags, den 10 mars, förra veckan, för två år sedan*) takes the past; no time, or "up to now", takes the perfect. Drill, 10 sentences, 5 of each:
1. *Jag beställde den i måndags.*
2. *Jag hyrde bilen den 10 mars.*
3. *Reparatören kom i fredags.*
4. *Jag har redan betalat.*
5. *Den har inte fungerat sedan i lördags.*
Then 5 more of your own, with this week's topics.

**Why it matters for the exam:** Complaints and reports always tell what happened and when, so a past-or-perfect error appears in almost every formal text.

- 0–6 Review: cards from Days 51, 67, 74, 78 and 80.

- **S3, complaint call** (6 turns, 20 s):
  - Card: *Du har köpt ett par vinterskor. Efter en vecka gick de sönder. Ring butiken. Förklara problemet och säg vad du vill.*
  - The other voice: 1. *Skobutiken, hej.* 2. *Vad gäller det?* 3. *När köpte du dem?* 4. *Har du kvittot kvar?* 5. *Vi kan skicka dem på reparation.* 6. *Okej, kom till butiken med skorna och kvittot.*
- **S4, voicemail** (20 s): *Du har en tid hos läkaren i morgon klockan tio, men du kan inte komma. Lämna ett meddelande.*
- **S5, three reactions** (20 s + 25 s each): a) *Din kollega berättar att hon ska gifta sig.* b) *Din vän har brutit benet.* c) *Din granne frågar om han kan låna din bil på lördag, men du behöver den själv.*
- **S6, opinion** (1 + 1.5 min): *Påstående: Alla borde lära sig laga mat i skolan. Håller du med? Motivera din åsikt.*

**Writing set (seen practice):**

| Task | Prompt | Required points |
|---|---|---|
| **W1, informal** | *Din vän ska besöka dig i Helsingfors. Föreslå en dag och en aktivitet, skriv var ni kan träffas och fråga vad din vän vill äta.* | 6: opening, day, activity, meeting place, food question, closing. |
| **W2, letter to the editor** | *Skriv en insändare: Alla borde åka kollektivt i stället för med bil. Skriv din åsikt och ge minst tre skäl.* | 8: topic line, opinion, reason 1, reason 2, reason 3, an example, other view, matching conclusion. |
| **W3, formal** | *Du har köpt en vattenkokare i en webbutik. Den är trasig. Skriv till butiken. Skriv när du köpte den, vad som är fel, vad du vill att butiken gör och ge dina kontaktuppgifter.* | 6: when bought (with order number), what is wrong, what you want, contact details, formal opening, formal closing. |

**Models (seen practice).**

W2:
> *Jag vill skriva om bilar i staden. Jag tycker att fler människor borde åka buss och tåg i stället för bil. För det första är det bättre för miljön. Bussar och tåg ger mindre utsläpp per person. För det andra sparar man pengar. Det kostar mycket att ha bil, till exempel bensin, försäkring och parkering. För det tredje blir det mindre trafik i centrum, och då blir luften renare. Å andra sidan är kollektivtrafiken inte bra överallt. På landet går bussen kanske bara två gånger om dagen. Men i staden är fördelarna större än nackdelarna. Därför tycker jag att man ska åka kollektivt när det är möjligt. Alex Kumar, Esbo*

S4:
> *Hej, det här är Alex Kumar. Jag har en tid i morgon klockan tio, men tyvärr kan jag inte komma. Kan jag få en ny tid nästa vecka? Ring mig gärna. Tack!* (about 30 words, which fits 20 seconds at a careful pace)

**Common errors on mock days:**

| Error | Fix |
|---|---|
| Only two reasons in W2 | The official sample asks for at least three. |
| No contact details or order number in W3 | Both are required points. |
| *För det tredje det blir …* | *För det tredje blir det …* |
| *Jag vet inte vad är fel.* | *Jag vet inte vad som är fel.* (In an indirect question, *vad* as the subject needs *som*.) |
| A voicemail over 20 seconds | Cut the reason to one short clause. |
| Stopping a call turn early because you missed the voice | Use one of the three recovery options: answer it if you understood it; answer the part you understood; or give the card's next piece of information without agreeing to anything (*Jag kan komma på fredag efter klockan fyra.*). Never say *Okej* by reflex. [Unreviewed Swedish: have a teacher check it] |

**Pass rules:** section 6.

---

label: After Day 84
title: After Day 84: the repeat cycle and the taper
markdown:
## After Day 84: the repeat cycle and the taper

### When this applies

- **Mock 3 alone cannot meet the booking gate.** The gate needs two full mocks in a row, at least one week apart, on fresh prompts, both passing 6.4 for the subtests you will book (4.7). So at least one more week always follows Day 84.
- **Section 4.6 sets the rule:** if the gate is not met after Day 84, repeat Days 64–84 with new prompts; do one full mock every week instead of every 4 weeks; after each mock, spend 3 fix days on that mock's top errors in the Day 57 format; keep cycling until the gate is met at a registration window.
- Phase 4 has no other exit. Its exit is the booking gate (4.5).

### The cycle week [Plan's own split of the 4.6 rule]

| Cycle day | What you do | Time |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Full mock** (6.2), fresh prompts, recorded and typed. The teacher rates first, then you count (6.3). | 2–2.5 h |
| 2 | **Fix day 1, Day 57 format** (error cards, engine drill, a speaking redo, a writing task, the log). Focus: say this mock's errors aloud, wrong then right; 2 new correct sentences for each top-3 error type; redo the weakest speaking task on a new card; one new text of the weakest written type (15 min). Mark red types (3.6). | 60 min |
| 3 | **Fix day 2, Day 57 format.** Focus: 3 four-minute drills built with the Day 67 recipe; redo the second-weakest speaking task and the weakest writing task with new details. | 60 min |
| 4 | **Fix day 3, Day 57 format.** Focus: the mock's weakest function, as on Day 58: the drill, then 3 speaking prompts and 1 writing prompt you have not practised (question-bank book tasks, or seen practice with the details changed). | 60 min |
| 5 | **Next day of the Phase 4 rotation** (below), with new prompts. | 60–80 min |
| 6 | **The day after it in the rotation.** | 60–80 min |
| 7 | **Light day** (3.1): due cards, one task re-recorded with a new detail, one clip; then the pre-mock warm-up (3.3: five random prompts from different engines, the 10 core reactions, the 12 core reason pairs). The helper prepares next week's mock. | 30–40 min |

- **The rotation** is the Phase 4 content days in order: 66, 69, 68, 74, 75, 80, 64 or 78, 65 or 79, then start again. New prompts for the rotation days come from the book map's question bank, or from seen practice with the details changed. The mock, fix and light days (67, 70–72, 76–77, 81–84) are already inside the cycle.
- If your target pair includes listening or reading, put Day 66 or 75 into every cycle week [Plan's own], because only teacher- or helper-written questions give booking evidence (6.2).
- Cards follow 3.3 as before. The mock day makes no new cards except error cards. The weekly teacher pack is the mock itself.

### Where the prompts come from

- **Every printed prompt is seen practice** (plan 6.2, decided 16 November 2026): the appendix, the plan's day entries and this file. Use them on fix days and rotation days with the details changed, never as a mock that counts.
- **Each weekly mock that counts needs fresh prompts,** from one of two sources, in this order (plan 6.2 as revised by the third review):
  1. **The teacher writes them** (or briefs a helper), one task per slot of the balanced mock recipe (6.2 and the teacher-only reserve file): S1 a person or an experience; S2 a seller call one week and a buyer call the next, with 6 voice lines; S3 a complaint or repair call with 6 voice lines; S4 a voicemail; S5 three reactions; S6 an opinion; W1 an informal message; W2 a letter with at least three reasons; W3 a formal complaint (a bill one week, a product the next); and the listening and reading items with about 8 questions each in the three formats.
  2. **Only as a fallback, an AI writes the prompts on the day,** one per slot; the helper reads them out, and the learner does not see them before the task.
- **The 40 held-back book tasks are not a source for counted mocks** any more: the learner's book map once described them, so they are seen practice. They stay in the teacher-only file `teacher-only/YKI-MOCK-RESERVE.md` for Mocks 1 and 2 and for spare practice on fix and rotation days.
- The learner never writes their own mock prompts.
- **Appendix prompts not yet used anywhere in this file** (still seen practice, but the least practised, so use them first on rotation and fix days): the Day 58 menu rows not used on Days 58, 59 or 76, plus A4, F7, F8, G1, G2, G4, G7, G9, I1, I4, I5, I7, I9, I10, J4 and J10. Almost none are seller, buyer or repair calls.
- **Close to tasks already done** (use them last): H10, K4, G5 and B5 (close to Mock 3), and A5, C7, E1, F9, G6, H1, I2, J2, J7, J8, K2, L1 and L6 (close to tasks in parts 1–3).

### After each weekly mock: the booking check (4.7)

1. Count the mock by 6.3; where your count and the teacher's differ, the teacher's stands.
2. Record Green, Amber or Red for each subtest in the mock table (Days 28, 56 and 84). Then compare with every row of 6.4 for the subtests you will book (the booking-gate checks, unchanged): every required point; every task in time; engine errors per text counted and tracked (not a pass rule); a teacher rating of A or B ("understandable with some errors" or better) on every task; about 70% or more on teacher- or helper-written listening or reading questions, if that subtest is in your pair. Write "pass" or "fail" and the date in the progress record.
3. The gate is met when **all** of these are true: two passes in a row, at least one week apart, on fresh prompts; both mocks within the 4 weeks before you pay [Plan's own]; Migri's written confirmation, if you plan to combine two partial-day certificates; every item of the 8.3 checklist ticked.
4. Choose what to book with the pair table in 4.7.
5. At each registration window listed in 4.7 (confirm every date and fee before paying), ask one question: **is the gate met today?** If not, let the window pass and keep cycling. Registration is binding [Official].

- With no outside rater you may not book (3.5).
- If the same function fails in two mocks running, spend one teacher session on it [Plan's own, extending the 4.3 rule for a function that fails twice].

### Phase 5: the 7-day taper (section 4.6)

Use it only in the last 7 days before a sitting you have **booked**, whatever the date. It replaces the cycle for those days: no mock and no fix days [Plan's own reading of 4.6]. Use old cards with one detail changed, or leftover appendix prompts. Nothing new is learned.

| Days before the test | Exactly what you do |
|---|---|
| 7 | One timed task of each type: Berätta about a person (1 min prep + 1.5 min); a seller call (6 turns × 20 s); a late voicemail (20 s); three reactions (20 s + 25 s each); W1, an informal message (15 min). All due cards. No new grammar, no new templates. About 60 min. |
| 6 | Berätta about an experience; a complaint or repair call; a cancel voicemail; three reactions; W3, a bill complaint with which bill, two reasons, an amount and contact details (20 min). All due cards. About 60 min. |
| 5 | Berätta about a place or your home; a buyer call; a late voicemail with a new reason; three reactions; W2, a letter with at least three reasons (25 min). All due cards. About 65 min. |
| 4 | Berätta about a person (a different one); a request or booking call; a cancel voicemail; three reactions; W3, a formal request with contact details (20 min). All due cards. About 60 min. |
| 3 | Berätta about an experience (a different one); a repair call; a voicemail; three reactions; your weakest written type from the last mock (15–25 min). All due cards. About 60 min. |
| 2 | Say the core frames aloud once (plan section 1). Do one short timed task (for example a 20-second voicemail). Pack valid photo ID: a passport, ID card or residence permit card, not a driving licence [Official]. About 25 min. |
| 1 | 20 minutes of light review only. Plan the journey with a time buffer: latecomers cannot sit the test [Official]. Pack food and water. Sleep. |
| Test day | Leave your phone and watch: devices are collected [Official]. Read every instruction twice. Answer every item. Never leave a task blank. |

- Days 7–3 are the 4.6 row "one timed task of each type per day". Spreading the three written types across those days is this part's choice [Plan's own].
- Keep the daily listening or reading routine on Days 7–3 (8 minutes on a 60-minute day, 10 on a 90-minute day); section 3.7 says not to skip it, and it is not new content. The taper days are a declared exception to load rule 5: one timed task of each type.
- If you are ill on the test morning: a refund is possible only for your own illness, with a medical certificate, if you cancel by 08:00 on the test morning [Official] (4.7).

*End of part 3. Before you drill any Swedish here, a teacher must check it.*
